adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,` around the shown diff). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code tries to add other hosts’ calendars via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional-chained `push` is skipped, so any collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are never attached to `evt` even when other collective hosts have `user.destinationCalendar`. This matches the finding’s claim that other hosts’ destination calendars get dropped in that scenario.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the `find(...)` branch runs), the predicate compares `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), which will not match normal destination calendars that have real `externalId`s. This makes the destinationCalendar fallback effectively dead and causes the code to proceed with an undefined calendar id (and likely fall back to default/primary behavior downstream), matching the finding.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute a fallback calendar id via `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. But in that branch `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so the `find(...)` predicate is effectively always false and returns `undefined`. In `deleteEvent`, this leads to falling back to `"primary"` (via `defaultCalendarId`) instead of using the event’s destination calendar when the reference doesn’t provide `externalCalendarId`, matching the finding’s claim about deleting from the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, the `else` branch for `!destination.credentialId` filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `c.type === destination.integration` and then does `Promise.all(...map(createEvent(c, event)))`. This ignores the specific `destination.externalId` and will create events for *every* credential of that integration type held by the EventManager (potentially multiple organizer creds), producing duplicates and not targeting the intended destination calendar when it can't be linked to a credential.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the recurring-series delete path is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` (where `bookingCalendarReference` is a `filter` result), so when there are multiple `_calendar` references it will rerun the recurring deletion logic for each reference (duplicating deletions). Additionally, within that recurring branch it iterates over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(..._calendar)` and for each `updBooking` it uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which only deletes the first calendar reference per updated booking. adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the PR builds evt.destinationCalendar as an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, pushes additional team members’ destination calendars (evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:316 — The deleteEvent fallback `find(cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it never matches and falls back to "primary"; the resulting 404 is silently resolved and legacy events on non-primary calendars are never deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. Because the `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), it compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it will not match any real calendar externalId and yields `undefined`. This effectively causes deletion to target the default calendar ("primary" / default fallback), breaking deletion of events that live on a non-primary destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — The updateEvent fallback has the same always-undefined `find`, so references without externalCalendarId send `calendarId: undefined` and the update rejects (it used to use the destination calendar).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback logic was changed from using `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null` (the common “no explicit externalCalendarId” case), the `find` predicate compares against `undefined`/`null` and returns `undefined`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. The subsequent `calendar.events.update` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` (no `|| "primary"` shown in the diff for update), which would send `calendarId: undefined` and cause the update to fail. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Credential (incl. OAuth key) loaded from DB by destinationCalendar.credentialId with no check that it belongs to a booking host/team member or is not invalid, bypassing the calendarCredentials allowlist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — Update path loads any credential by bookingReference.credentialId without ownership or invalid-flag checks, allowing use of another user's calendar credential on reschedule.
